## `AssetFormat`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Loaders.AssetFormat` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

File encoding as recognised by [`FileKindDetector`](#filekinddetector). Only [`AssetFormat.Png`](#assetformat--png), [`AssetFormat.Wav`](#assetformat--wav) and [`AssetFormat.OggVorbis`](#assetformat--oggvorbis) can be loaded; [`AssetFormat.Jpeg`](#assetformat--jpeg) exists solely so a JPEG can be rejected by name instead of as "unrecognised header", which is the single most likely mistake in a hand-made pack.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="assetformat--unknown"></a>`Unknown` | 0 | Header (or extension) matched nothing known. |
| <a id="assetformat--png"></a>`Png` | 1 | PNG image. Loadable. |
| <a id="assetformat--wav"></a>`Wav` | 2 | RIFF/WAVE audio. Loadable (16-bit PCM only, see [`WavParser`](#wavparser)). |
| <a id="assetformat--oggvorbis"></a>`OggVorbis` | 3 | Ogg container, assumed Vorbis. Loadable through the engine's decoder only. |
| <a id="assetformat--jpeg"></a>`Jpeg` | 4 | JPEG image. Recognised, never loaded. |

<a id="assetkey"></a>

## `AssetKey`

struct · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Loaders.AssetKey` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Implements: `IEquatable<AssetKey>`

A pack file addressed the way the rest of the framework wants it: a normalised forward-slash path, plus the bare [`AssetKey.Name`](#assetkey--name) the game will see.

[`AssetKey.Name`](#assetkey--name) is load-bearing, not cosmetic. Texture replacement assigns the loaded `Texture2D.name` to a lilToon material slot and voice replacement registers an `AudioClip` into KanKikuchi's `VoiceManager` cache *by clip name*, where the game's own keys are plain names such as `Voice_Tutorial_1_001`. So the file `audio/voice/Voice_Tutorial_1_001.ogg` must yield exactly `Voice_Tutorial_1_001`, with no folder, no extension and no case change.

<a id="assetkey--extension"></a>

### `string Extension { get; }`

Extension including the dot, lower-cased (`.png`), or empty when there is none. Lower-cased because it is only ever compared against a fixed set of known extensions; [`AssetKey.Name`](#assetkey--name) and [`AssetKey.Path`](#assetkey--path) keep the author's casing.

<a id="assetkey--name"></a>

### `string Name { get; }`

File name without its extension - the name the game will address the asset by. A leading dot is not an extension, so `.keep` has the name `.keep`, and only the last extension is removed, so `Voice.v2.ogg` has the name `Voice.v2`.

<a id="assetkey--path"></a>

### `string Path { get; }`

The normalised path: backslashes turned into `/`, repeated separators collapsed, `.` segments dropped. A leading `/` is preserved, and `..` segments are deliberately *not* resolved - this type normalises spelling, it does not walk a file system.

<a id="assetkey--equals-assetkey"></a>

### `bool Equals(AssetKey other)`

Two keys are equal when their normalised paths are, byte for byte.

Ordinal on purpose: macOS is case-insensitive and Windows is too, but the game's clip and texture names are case-sensitive, so a key that only differs in case addresses a different asset as far as the framework is concerned.

<a id="filekinddetector"></a>

## `FileKindDetector`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Loaders.FileKindDetector` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Decides what a pack file is, from its extension and the first few bytes of its content.

Content wins over extension whenever both are available. A pack is hand-made: a file is far more often renamed than re-encoded, so the bytes are the truth and a mismatched extension is a note on an otherwise successful detection, not a failure. With no bytes to look at the extension is all there is, and the reason string says so.

<a id="filekinddetector--headerbytes"></a>

### `const int HeaderBytes = 16`

How many leading bytes are enough for every signature here. A caller that streams a file only needs this much of it (12 are actually used; 16 is a round number with room).

<a id="filekinddetector--detect"></a>

### `static FileKindDetection Detect(string path, byte[] firstBytes = null)`

Detects the format of `path`.

**Parameters**

- `path`: Path to the file. Only its spelling is used - nothing is read from disk, which is what keeps this type Unity-free and unit-testable.
- `firstBytes`: The first [`FileKindDetector.HeaderBytes`](#filekinddetector--headerbytes) bytes of the file, or null/empty when the caller has not read the file yet. More bytes than that are fine; fewer are used as far as they go.

**Returns:** Never null. Check [`FileKindDetection.Supported`](#filekinddetection--supported) before loading.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `path` is blank or has no file name.

## `LoadReport`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Loaders.LoadReport` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Everything one run of the loaders did, file by file. Aggregation lives here, once, so the log line, the smoke detail and the unit tests cannot disagree about how many files loaded.

Every member takes the same lock. The loaders run on Unity's main thread, but the async audio path finishes in a coroutine callback several frames after the call that started it, and a pack load that is still in flight while a report is being summarised must not throw.

<a id="loadreport--nothingloadedsummary"></a>

### `const string NothingLoadedSummary = "no files loaded"`

[`LoadReport.Summarize`](#loadreport--summarize) when nothing was attempted.

<a id="loadreport--count"></a>

### `int Count { get; }`

How many files were attempted.

<a id="loadreport--entries"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<LoadEntry> Entries { get; }`

Entries in the order they were added.

A detached copy: adding to the report never mutates a list a caller is reading.

<a id="loadreport--failures"></a>

Entries that did not load, in order.

<a id="loadreport--ok"></a>

### `bool Ok { get; }`

True when at least one file was attempted and every one of them loaded. An empty report is not ok: it proves nothing, exactly like an empty smoke run.

<a id="loadreport--add"></a>

### `void Add(LoadEntry entry)`

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `entry` is null.

<a id="loadreport--clear"></a>

### `void Clear()`

Forgets every entry. Used between runs and by tests.

<a id="loadreport--countof"></a>

### `int CountOf(AssetKind kind)`

How many entries of this kind were recorded, loaded or not.

<a id="loadreport--summarize"></a>

### `string Summarize()`

One line fit for LogOutput.log or a smoke detail, e.g. `4 file(s): 3 ok, 1 failed; 2 texture, 2 audio; 9216 bytes; 21 ms`.

Invariant culture, so the string is the same on every machine and in every test.

<a id="wavdata--ctor"></a>

### `WavData(int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample, float[] samples)`

Creates decoded WAV data.

**Parameters**

- `channels`: 1 or more interleaved channels.
- `sampleRate`: Frames per second, e.g. 44100.
- `bitsPerSample`: Bit depth of the source file; always 16 for now.

<a id="wavparser"></a>

## `WavParser`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Loaders.WavParser` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A small, strict RIFF/WAVE reader for 16-bit PCM. Pure C#, so the WAV path is covered by unit tests rather than only by a launch of the game.

Deliberately narrow: packs are our own files, 16-bit PCM is what every editor exports by default, and a decoder that silently handled six bit depths would be six times the code and six times the ways to be subtly wrong about loudness. Anything else is refused by name so the fix is obvious. Ogg is not decoded here at all - the engine does that (see `AudioLoader.LoadAsync`).

<a id="wavparser--supportedbitspersample"></a>

### `const int SupportedBitsPerSample = 16`

The only bit depth that can be decoded.

<a id="wavparser--parse"></a>

### `static WavData Parse(byte[] bytes)`

Decodes a WAV file.

**Parameters**

- `bytes`: The whole file.

**Returns:** The decoded samples and their format.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `bytes` is null.
- [`WavFormatException`](#wavformatexception): The file is not a 16-bit PCM WAV we can read.

<a id="wavparser--tryparse"></a>

### `static bool TryParse(byte[] bytes, out WavData data, out string error)`

Decodes a WAV file without throwing - the shape a per-file loader wants.

**Parameters**

- `bytes`: The whole file, or null.
- `data`: The decoded data, or null on failure.
- `error`: The reason on failure, or null on success.

**Returns:** True when `data` was produced.

<a id="wavwriter"></a>

## `WavWriter`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Loaders.WavWriter` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Produces canonical 44-byte-header 16-bit PCM WAV files.

This exists so the WAV path can be proved without shipping a binary fixture: the unit tests round-trip [`WavWriter.Write`](#wavwriter--write) through [`WavParser`](#wavparser), and the in-game smoke checks synthesise a tone with [`WavWriter.Tone`](#wavwriter--tone) and load it back through the engine. It is not a general-purpose encoder and does not need to be.

<a id="wavwriter--headerbytes"></a>

### `const int HeaderBytes = 44`

Size of the canonical RIFF/fmt /data header this writer emits.

<a id="wavwriter--tone"></a>

### `static byte[] Tone(double frequencyHz, double seconds, int sampleRate = 44100, int channels = 1, float amplitude = 0.5f)`

Synthesises a sine tone as a 16-bit PCM WAV file. Used by the smoke checks and the unit tests; it is the "known good audio" no fixture file has to be shipped for.

**Parameters**

- `frequencyHz`: Tone frequency, e.g. 440.
- `seconds`: Length; rounded to the nearest whole frame.
- `sampleRate`: Frames per second. Defaults to 44100.
- `channels`: Interleaved channel count; every channel gets the same tone.
- `amplitude`: Peak amplitude in 0..1.

**Returns:** The complete file.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: An argument is out of range.

<a id="wavwriter--write"></a>

### `static byte[] Write(float[] samples, int channels, int sampleRate)`

Encodes interleaved samples as a 16-bit PCM WAV file.

**Parameters**

- `samples`: Interleaved samples. Values outside -1..1 are clamped rather than allowed to wrap, because a wrapped sample is a loud click and a clamped one is merely flat.
- `channels`: Interleaved channel count; 1 or more.
- `sampleRate`: Frames per second, e.g. 44100.

**Returns:** The complete file.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `samples` is null.
- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: A count or rate is not positive.
- `ArgumentException`: The sample count is not a whole number of frames.
